newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHIPYARD HOLDING GROUP TO BE READY OCT 15.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHIPYARD HOLDING GROUP TO BE READY OCT 15.

text.p: Poland's economy minister said on Tuesday the delayed creation of a shipbuilding holding group, designed to help the industry survive foreign competition, was likely to be completed by October 15.
"All procedures necessary for setting up the holding should be completed by October 15," the minister, Wieslaw Kaczmarek, told a news briefing.
The holding is to group the successful Szczecin shipyard which will take over stakes in the less prosperous Gdynia yard, the troubled ship-engine maker H. Cegielski and possibly other firms.

Earlier this year, Finance Minister Marek Belka, tired of waiting for a result from talks among the group's would-be members, decided to kick-start the plan by trying to give the state treasury's 46 percent stake in Gdynia over to Szczecin's management.
But Kaczmarek said the handover had proved impossible under the Polish commercial code and prospective members would have to set up the group by themselves.
"The holding's prospective members want to join the group provided that relations inside it will be that of partners and not that of master and servant," he said.
Gdynia officials earlier said they feared their company would lose independence in the group.

Under the shipyard sector consolidation plan, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) would buy a new share issue of Szczecin so as to provide it with funds to buy Gdynia's new stock issue, which may double its capital.
Last month, Gdynia's shareholders approved a new share issue of between 45 and 151 million zlotys, which may be taken over by Szczecin.

In the Szczecin shipyard, employees now have 34.7 percent of shares, a group of four Polish banks has 30 percent, with 15 percent in the hands of Capital Group Ltd, 9 percent owned by the management and 5.3 percent by small shareholders.

Apart from the treasury's 46 percent stake in Gdynia, other shareholders include the state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA which has 20.5 percent of shares and Bank Handlowy with 18.7 percent.
The government says creation of the holding is the industry's only chance to weather foreign competition in the longer term. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
